claims.text: The initially solid FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles are homogeneous and have a uniform elemental distribution.
Surface segregation of a lower-melting constituent governs the phase transition of FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles.
Cu is likely the lower-melting constituent responsible for the proposed segregation.
Cu segregates to the nanoparticle surface during heating.
Heating produces a Cu-enriched surface layer or compositional gradient.
Cu enrichment locally lowers the melting point at the nanoparticle surface.
The locally reduced melting point creates a liquid-like premelting layer at the surface.
The surface liquid-like layer facilitates progression of melting into the nanoparticle core as temperature increases.
Melting will initiate at the nanoparticle surface before bulk melting.
Cu surface enrichment will precede the onset of bulk melting.
The baseline nanoparticles are crystalline and compositionally homogeneous.
The baseline nanoparticles exhibit no surface melting or segregation below the overall bulk melting temperature.
The proposed premelting behavior is expected under inert high-temperature conditions below complete bulk melting.
Keeping the nanoparticle size distribution consistent minimizes size-related effects on the observed transition.
Using an inert atmosphere prevents oxidation during heating.
Absence of preferential Cu surface segregation together with retention of a uniform crystalline structure until bulk melting would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The baseline states that the nanoparticles exhibit no surface melting or segregation below the overall bulk melting temperature, whereas the hypothesis predicts Cu segregation and surface premelting in that same sub-bulk-melting regime. This is only consistent if the baseline is explicitly restricted to the initial low-temperature state.
